title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript note. It is a page of a typed Bourbaki draft, marked '4 - 34 - n° 392' (a Bourbaki redaction number), filed among the L-function notes. Its content is the 'restriction of scalars' statement for divisors and modules from the draft of Algèbre commutative, ch. VII (Diviseurs), §4.

Setting: A is a Noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K. L is a finite extension of K, and B is the integral closure of A in L, assumed finite over A. R is a finitely generated B-module and R_[A] denotes R viewed as an A-module. Let a = Ann_A(R) and b = Ann_B(R), so a = b ∩ A. The first lines finish a preliminary remark: since B is integral over A, 0 is the only ideal of B lying over 0, so a ≠ 0 if and only if b ≠ 0. Hence R is torsion if and only if R_[A] is torsion.

(i) R is pseudo-null over B if and only if R_[A] is pseudo-null over A.
- If b ⊂ P with P a height-1 prime of B, then a ⊂ P ∩ A = p, which has height 1.
- Conversely, if a ⊂ p with p a height-1 prime of A, lying-over / going-up gives a prime P ⊃ b over p.
- One then applies the criterion of n°4, Prop. 9: a torsion module is pseudo-null if and only if no height-1 prime contains its annihilator.

(ii) For torsion R, set φ(R) = χ_A(R_[A]). By (i), φ is additive and kills pseudo-null modules, so by n°5, Prop. 11 it factors as φ = θ∘χ_B for a homomorphism θ: D(B) → D(A). It suffices to compute θ on the modules B/P, since χ_B(B/P) = P.
- For a height-1 prime q ≠ p = P ∩ A, q is not contained in P, so (B/P)_q = 0.
- (B/P)_p = κ(P), and its length as an A_p-module is the residue degree f_{P/p}.
- Hence θ = N, the norm of divisors (n°5, Def. 4): χ_A(R_[A]) = N(χ_B(R)).

(iii) Formula (21): rank_A(R_[A]) = [L:K]·rank_B(R). Torsion submodules are compatible with restriction of scalars, so one reduces to R torsion-free. Then R sits inside R⊗L. If e_i is an L-basis of R⊗L contained in R and b_j is a K-basis of L contained in B, the products b_j e_i form a K-basis of R⊗K contained in R.

The page breaks off at the start of a further statement about a sub-B-module M. It serves the general theory of divisors and characteristic divisors χ, which is the background for Iwasawa-type and L-function considerations.
errors: No mathematical errors. Implicit hypotheses are needed: B must be finite over A for R_[A] to be finitely generated (e.g. L/K separable, or A Japanese).
'P ∩ A = p is of height 1' uses going-down for an integral extension of a normal domain; this is cited only implicitly.
The page is unrelated to the neighbouring handwritten pages (Artin representations; cohomology at infinity). It is an inserted Bourbaki typescript.

ideas.what: Restriction of scalars preserves torsion and pseudo-nullity for integral extensions of normal Noetherian domains
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative, ch. VII, §4 (restriction of scalars)

ideas.what: χ_A(R_[A]) = N(χ_B(R)): the characteristic divisor commutes with the norm
ideas.modern_name: norm of divisors / pushforward of cycles, degree f_{P/p}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki (classical; cf. Fulton's proper pushforward of cycles)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft page (redaction n°392) of standard material on divisors, later published in Algèbre commutative ch. VII. It contains nothing original to Grothendieck and nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The header 'n° 392' is a Bourbaki redaction number, not part of the mathematics.
Underlined letters (a, b, p, P, q) are Bourbaki's notation for ideals; the transcription renders them correctly.
